Hypothesis: We hypothesize that in liver neoplasms, increased MAP3K2 expression, when acting in tandem with RAS/RAF kinases, directly phosphorylates critical subunits of the geranylgeranyl transferase complex. The phosphorylation alters the complex’s activity, leading to aberrant geranylgeranylation of small GTPases such as Rho proteins. This modification disrupts cell adhesion and migration, thereby contributing to a metastasis-prone phenotype. Importantly, this MAP3K2-driven mechanism acts synergistically with well-established oncogenic signals—including the TAM-derived GDNF-GFRA1 survival axis, modest increments in Met RTK expression that drive tumor initiation, and MAPT-mediated autophagy inhibition—to amplify the aggressive behavior of liver tumors. To validate this hypothesis, we will employ advanced technologies: CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing to generate phosphorylation-resistant variants of geranylgeranyl transferase subunits; high-throughput phosphoproteomics to confirm and map phosphorylation events; live-cell imaging to track dynamic changes in cell adhesion and motility; and single-cell transcriptomics to attribute pathway-specific expression changes within heterogeneous tumor cell populations.
Abstract: In liver neoplasms, our refined hypothesis posits that elevated MAP3K2 expression cooperates with RAS/RAF kinases to induce direct phosphorylation of specific subunits within the geranylgeranyl transferase complex. This event impairs the enzymatic capacity to modify critical small GTPases (e.g., Rho proteins), thereby disrupting normal cell adhesion and migration. Acting in concert with established oncogenic pathways such as the TAM-derived GDNF-GFRA1 survival axis, subtle wild-type Met receptor tyrosine kinase dosage effects, and MAPT-mediated autophagy inhibition, this pathway synergistically enhances metastatic potential. Leveraging state-of-the-art technologies—including CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing to create phosphorylation-resistant mutants, high-throughput phosphoproteomic mapping to precisely index kinase-substrate interactions, live-cell imaging to monitor cell migratory behavior, and single-cell transcriptomics to dissect heterogeneity in pathway activation—we aim to delineate the direct mechanistic impact of MAP3K2-mediated modifications in liver cancer metastasis.
CausalChain: MAP3K2 upregulation -> Enhanced MAP3K2-RAS/RAF cooperation -> Direct phosphorylation of geranylgeranyl transferase complex components -> Impaired geranylgeranylation of small GTPases -> Disruption of cell adhesion/migration -> Synergistic enhancement of metastasis
